headlines.title: Bloomberg Economist: ‘This Was All About Oil’ and Compares Chevron’s Venezuela Deal to 1953 Iran Coup
headlines.summary: A Bloomberg economist just compared Chevron's blockbuster Venezuela oil deal to a Cold War coup that looked like a triumph for 25 years before costing the U.S. one of its biggest crude suppliers almost overnight. History has a pattern here, and CVX shareholders paying a 52-week-high price may not be priced for it.

headlines.summary: The oil giant is expanding its Venezuelan operations with plans to more than double production.

headlines.title: Who Really Got Rights to Venezuela’s 65 Billion Barrels Of Oil Prize?
headlines.summary: Washington just handed a 100-year lease on tens of billions of barrels of Venezuelan oil to a private company nobody has heard of, while Chevron quietly hit a 52-week high on a completely separate deal. The two stories are getting conflated in ways that could cost investors.

headlines.title: 3 of Wall Street’s Safest High-Yield Dividend Stocks With Over 25-Year Increase Streaks
headlines.summary: Not all Dividend Aristocrats are created equal, and three companies spanning payroll processing, supplemental insurance, and integrated energy have quietly stacked 25-plus years of annual raises through completely different cash engines.

description: Chevron Corporation, through its subsidiaries, engages in the integrated energy and chemicals operations in the United States and internationally. It operates through Upstream and Downstream segments. The Upstream segment engages in the exploration for, development, production, and transportation of crude oil and natural gas; processing, liquefaction, transportation, and regasification of liquefied natural gas; transportation of crude oil through pipelines; transportation, storage, and marketing of natural gas; carbon capture and storage; and operation of a gas-to-liquids plant. Its Downstream segment refines crude oil into petroleum products; markets crude oil, refined products, and lubricants; manufactures and markets renewable fuels; transports crude oil and refined products through pipeline, marine vessel, motor equipment, and rail car; and manufactures and markets commodity petrochemicals, plastics for industrial uses, and fuel and lubricant additives. It has operations in North America, South America, Europe, Africa, Asia, and Australia. The company was formerly known as ChevronTexaco Corporation and changed its name to Chevron Corporation in May 2005. Chevron Corporation was founded in 1879 and is headquartered in Houston, Texas.
